sections.title: How it wins
sections.text: Toph does not win alone: with her, every nontoken artifact is also a land, so each artifact you cast is a landfall trigger, and the land she animates with her earthbend 2 at each end step returns to the battlefield when it dies or is exiled (another landfall). The plan is to play 2 to 4 lands per turn from turn 3 and turn each landfall into 1 damage to EACH opponent: Sabotender and Tannuk for every land, Arbaaz Mir for each legendary creature or artifact that enters, and Valakut Exploration in your end step. Ragost (3 to each opponent per sacrificed artifact), Fire Nation Archers ({5}: 2 to each opponent), Legion Guildmage ({5}{R}: 3 to each opponent) and Goblin Bombardment spend the leftover mana and artifacts, while Tireless Tracker, Terrasymbiosis, Stocking the Pantry, Valakut and Tannuk refill your hand. The Stasis Coffin animated by Toph makes you untouchable on each opponent's turn for {2}, so the drain has the turns it needs. If a loop comes together (Springheart Nantuko with Lotus Cobra or Tireless Provisioner; Toph, Hardheaded Teacher with Gruul Turf and Zuran Orb; Ashaya with Toph, the Blind Bandit), any pinger kills the whole table at once. Backup: the army of animated lands (The Earth King, Seismic Tutelage on Secret Tunnel, Bumi), which returns after creature board wipes. Realistically: the drain alone kills around turns 10 to 12, the army knocks out a player around turn 8 or 9, and a loop shows up around turn 7 in 1 game out of 7.

sections.title: Mulligan
sections.text: Keep 2 to 4 lands (2 only with a ramp spell costing 2 mana or less; 5 only with a play costing 3 or less), a play by turn 2 or 3, and a piece of the plan or a way to find it; Toph counts as a piece if the mana for turn 3 or 4 is in hand. Almost any hand with good lands is a keep if it has Sol Ring, Lotus Cobra, a pinger (Sabotender, Arbaaz Mir, Tannuk), Tireless Tracker or Terrasymbiosis. Look for green: 34 spells need it, and almost all the early ramp costs {1}{G}. Before Toph, artifacts are not lands: don't count Mishra's Bauble or Zuran Orb as lands in hand. Mulligan with 0 or 1 land (even if it has Sol Ring), with 6 or more lands, with 2 lands and no cheap ramp, with no play before turn 4, or with only answers. With the free mulligan you keep in about 9 of every 10 games.

sections.title: Turn by turn
sections.text: T1: Sol Ring, Wayfarer's Bauble, Stocking the Pantry or Hardened Scales; otherwise, the land that enters tapped (never Gruul Turf as your only land). T2: ramp for {1}{G} (Rampant Growth, Shared Roots, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Lotus Cobra, Great Divide Guide, Druid Class), or a Talisman or Arcane Signet for Toph on turn 3; with a rock already on the battlefield, a 2-mana pinger (Sabotender, Arbaaz Mir). T3: Toph; if she doesn't come down, an engine (Tireless Tracker, Tireless Provisioner, Tannuk, Terrasymbiosis, Earthbender Ascension, Heaped Harvest). T4: a pinger and land ramp; with Toph on the battlefield, cheap artifacts go AFTER the pingers, because each one is a landfall. T5: another engine (Valakut Exploration, Terrasymbiosis), or The Stasis Coffin with {2} free to activate it. T6 to T9: 3 to 4 landfalls per turn, Ragost in each end step, Clues and Stocking the Pantry with the leftover mana, Fire Nation Archers with the rest, and build a loop behind Redirect Lightning or Collective Resistance. Harrow, Cycle of Renewal and the fetches are used at the end of the turn of the opponent before you, or on your turn with the pingers already on the battlefield.

sections.title: When to cast Toph
sections.text: On turn 3 or 4 (in colors she comes down on turn 3 in half the games, and by around turn 4 in 9 of every 10). If you have a pinger and Toph wouldn't come down a turn earlier, cast the pinger first, and keep the cheap artifacts in hand for after her: artifacts already in play become lands when Toph arrives, but they don't trigger landfall. Her value is in the end step, so decide ahead which land you'll earthbend: The Stasis Coffin if someone can damage you; a Forest if you have Springheart Nantuko in hand and Cobra or Provisioner in play; Gruul Turf with Toph, Hardheaded Teacher and Zuran Orb in play; otherwise Heaped Harvest, Solemn Simulacrum, Mishra's Bauble, Soul-Guide Lantern, Wayfarer's Bauble, an uncracked fetch, Urza's Cave or Haywire Mite; and Secret Tunnel for the army. Never earthbend Ashaya, Bumi or Brightglass Gearhulk: they're left as 0/0 creatures plus the counters. Toph never attacks; with Great Divide Guide in play she also taps for mana of any color (she's an Ally). If an opponent has removal open, cast her with Collective Resistance, Origin of Metalbending or Redirect Lightning ready; recasting her costs 6, then 8, and the deck's ramp pays for it.

sections.title: When to attack and when to wait
sections.text: This deck wins without combat: Toph, the pingers (Sabotender, Tannuk, Arbaaz Mir, Ragost), Tireless Tracker and Lotus Cobra are worth more alive and don't attack. Attack with animated lands only when it's free: if they die they return tapped, and that's a landfall, but attacking taps them and takes away their mana and their blocks. Attack for real when The Earth King fetches a basic for each attacker with power 4 or more (the Bear, Gearhulk, Bumi, a land animated twice or one with Hardened Scales), when Seismic Tutelage is on an animated Secret Tunnel, or when Bumi can connect. Earthbender Ascension (from the fourth landfall on) gives trample, and Secret Tunnel ({4}, tap) makes two creatures that share a type unblockable (Bumi and The Earth King are Humans). Wait if the counterattack would kill you and you don't have the Coffin ready or blockers: your animated lands are your best defense, because they block and return. Attack the opponent with no blockers or the one who is ahead; the drain already hits everyone.

sections.title: Tutors and what to look for
sections.text: Chord of Calling is an instant: cast it at the end of the turn of the opponent before you, with convoke from animated lands, Archers' Soldiers and green creatures. X=1 Haywire Mite as a response; X=2 Lotus Cobra (loop A), Sabotender, Arbaaz Mir, Ragost or Legion Guildmage; X=3 Tireless Provisioner (loop A), Tannuk, Tireless Tracker or Toph, the Blind Bandit (loop C); X=4 Fire Nation Archers, The Earth King, Solemn Simulacrum or Toph, Hardheaded Teacher; X=5 Ashaya or Bumi. Never search for Springheart Nantuko with Chord: it enters without attaching and doesn't set up the loop. Seismic Sense looks at as many cards as you have lands (with Toph, artifacts count too): use it from 6 lands to find a pinger, Nantuko, the loop piece you're missing or Gruul Turf. Crop Rotation (Game Changer) sacrifices the animated land, which returns, and fetches Gruul Turf (loop B), Urza's Cave, Secret Tunnel or Ba Sing Se, untapped; Urza's Cave ({3}) fetches any land and, if it's animated, repeats that every turn. Brightglass Gearhulk fetches up to two of: Zuran Orb, Mishra's Bauble, Hardened Scales, Stocking the Pantry, Sol Ring, Soul-Guide Lantern, Wayfarer's Bauble or Haywire Mite. Order: with no pinger, a pinger; with a loop half-built, the missing piece; otherwise, an engine (Tracker, Provisioner, Tannuk).

sections.title: Graveyard
sections.text: There's no reanimation: what comes back is what Toph animated, and it returns straight to the battlefield when it dies or is exiled, without going through the graveyard as a resource. On entering, Toph, Hardheaded Teacher lets you discard a card to return an instant or sorcery: Harrow, Crop Rotation, Chord of Calling, Swords to Plowshares, Beast Within, Chaos Warp or Planar Outburst; discard a spare land or a late ramp spell. Wrenn and Realmbreaker's −2 mills three and lets you take a permanent from only those three. Soul-Guide Lantern is your graveyard hate: on entering it exiles the card an opponent wants to reanimate, and when sacrificed it exiles every opponent's graveyard; animated by Toph it returns, and its enter trigger exiles another card. Drannith Magistrate stops opponents from casting spells from the graveyard, from exile or from the command zone.

sections.title: What to protect against
sections.text: 1) Combat damage and spells that target you: The Stasis Coffin animated by Toph gives you protection from everything on each opponent's turn for {2}. 2) Removal on Toph, a pinger or a loop piece: Redirect Lightning changes the target of any spell or ability with a single target, Collective Resistance gives hexproof and indestructible, and Origin of Metalbending gives indestructible; against an exile effect only Collective Resistance and Redirect Lightning work. 3) Creature board wipes: Make a Stand in response, or sacrifice to Goblin Bombardment whatever is about to die; the animated lands return, and Valakut, Terrasymbiosis, Stocking the Pantry and Bombardment stay. 4) Mass artifact removal: with Toph your artifacts are lands and fall together, including the Coffin if it isn't animated yet; in response, sacrifice them to Zuran Orb or Ragost, or use them for Harrow or Crop Rotation. 5) Fast opposing combo: you have no counterspells, so keep instant-speed removal and Haywire Mite for their turn, and cast Drannith Magistrate early. 6) What the Coffin doesn't stop: life loss ('each opponent loses'), mill, effects without a target, blocked searches (Aven Mindcensor) and land destruction.

sections.title: Removal priorities
sections.text: Swords to Plowshares and Path to Exile cost 1: save them for the commander or the engine that's beating you, never for a big creature that the Coffin or an animated blocker already handles (Path to Exile is better late, when one more land doesn't matter to the opponent). From turn 5, leave an instant open on the opponents' turns (Beast Within, Chaos Warp, Stroke of Midnight, Fateful Absence) for a combo piece. Against artifacts and enchantments, first Haywire Mite (if it's animated, it returns), then the 3-mana instants, and the destroy mode of Collective Resistance or Origin of Metalbending only if you don't need the shield that turn. Annie Joins Up deals 5 to a creature or planeswalker and also doubles the triggers of Toph, Tannuk and Arbaaz Mir: use it when both things matter. Cast Drannith Magistrate early against tables that depend on their commander. In a 4-player pod the drain is visible: point your removal at the leader, and don't spend it on what only threatens another player.

sections.title: When to clear the board
sections.text: Planar Outburst ({3}{W}{W}) destroys only the creatures that aren't lands: your animated lands survive, and so do Solemn Simulacrum, Haywire Mite and Brightglass Gearhulk with Toph on the battlefield (they're lands), and with Ashaya all your nontoken creatures. Without Ashaya, Toph and your pingers die, so use it only when you're behind on board. Ideally cast Make a Stand first: your creatures become indestructible and only the opponents' creatures die; otherwise, sacrifice to Goblin Bombardment whatever you're going to lose. With 8 mana, awaken puts four counters on a land: choose one that's already animated, so that Terrasymbiosis draws 4 (5 with Hardened Scales) and leaves a big attacker for The Earth King. Against many small tokens it isn't needed: the drain ignores blockers, and the Coffin stops their attack.

combos.title: Toph + The Stasis Coffin (a shield every turn)
combos.meta: Protection from everything on each opponent's turn · 2 cards with Toph · {3} once, then {2} per turn
combos.text:
Needs: Toph on the battlefield; The Stasis Coffin on the battlefield (with Toph it's also a land); {2} free in your end step. It does not win by itself: it leaves you untouchable while the drain works.
At the beginning of your end step, aim Toph's earthbend 2 at the Coffin: it becomes animated with haste and will return if it's exiled.
With that trigger resolved, hold priority and activate the Coffin ({2}, tap, exile it): you have protection from everything until your next turn.
The Coffin returns tapped right away: it's a landfall (Sabotender, Tannuk, Valakut) and a legendary artifact entering (Arbaaz Mir: 1 to each opponent and 1 life).
On opponents' turns, all damage to you is prevented and nobody can target you; your permanents and Wrenn stay exposed.
It untaps in your untap step: repeat it in each end step. With Annie Joins Up or Toph, Hardheaded Teacher you get a second earthbend for a valuable artifact the same turn.
Saving the {2} until the attack or the spell that matters saves mana, but an opponent can destroy or exile the Coffin first: it comes back tapped, and that cycle doesn't protect you. If in doubt, activate it in your own end step.
It doesn't stop life loss, mill or effects without a target; and artifact removal before you animate it means losing it for good.

combos.title: Loop A: Springheart Nantuko + Lotus Cobra or Tireless Provisioner
combos.meta: Infinite landfall · 3 cards with Toph · {1}{G} for bestow + {1}{G} for the first copy
combos.text:
Needs: an animated basic land (Toph's earthbend; also Earthbender Ascension, Ba Sing Se, Toph, the Blind Bandit or Toph, Hardheaded Teacher); Springheart Nantuko in hand, cast with bestow (never with Chord of Calling); Lotus Cobra or Tireless Provisioner on the battlefield; {1}{G} + {1}{G}; a pinger (Sabotender, Tannuk) or Valakut Exploration, or Fire Nation Archers if you have both Cobra AND Provisioner.
In your end step Toph animates a basic Forest (any basic works; the Forest provides the green).
In your next main phase, cast Springheart Nantuko with bestow ({1}{G}) on that animated Forest.
Start with a landfall: play a land, crack a fetch or cast a cheap artifact.
Each landfall triggers Nantuko and Cobra (or Provisioner): order them so Cobra resolves first and its mana stays floating.
When Nantuko's trigger resolves, pay {1}{G}: create a token copy of the Forest. The copy is a normal Forest, enters untapped and is another landfall.
Cobra gives you a mana (or Provisioner a Treasure), and you tap the token for {G}: that pays for the next {1}{G}. Repeat: each cycle is a free landfall.
Sabotender and Tannuk deal 1 to each opponent per cycle; Tireless Tracker makes Clues and Druid Class gains life. With Cobra and Provisioner together, 1 mana is left over per cycle: infinite mana for Fire Nation Archers ({5}: 2 to each opponent) without a pinger.
To stop it, don't pay: Nantuko creates a 1/1 Insect. With Valakut in play, each cycle exiles your top card, and the damage comes in your end step: don't empty your library if that damage won't kill.

combos.title: Loop B: Toph + Toph, Hardheaded Teacher + Gruul Turf + Zuran Orb
combos.meta: Infinite landfall, life and casts · 4 cards with Toph · {0} per cycle, only in your main phase
combos.text:
Needs: Toph and Toph, Hardheaded Teacher on the battlefield; Gruul Turf on the battlefield and animated (by Toph's earthbend, or by Toph, Hardheaded Teacher's trigger when you cast any spell); Zuran Orb on the battlefield; your main phase with an empty stack, because the Orb is cast as an artifact. Variant: Goblin Bombardment as the sacrifice outlet and Mishra's Bauble as the {0} artifact.
Sacrifice Gruul Turf to Zuran Orb: you gain 2 life.
Gruul Turf returns tapped (a landfall), and its trigger makes you return a land to hand: return Zuran Orb, which is a land under Toph.
Cast Zuran Orb for {0}. Toph, Hardheaded Teacher's trigger (earthbend 1) resolves before the Orb: aim it at Gruul Turf.
The Orb enters: another landfall, and an artifact entering (Arbaaz Mir: 1 to each opponent).
Repeat: each cycle is 2 landfalls, 2 life and one cast; with Sabotender, Tannuk or Arbaaz Mir on the battlefield the whole table dies, and Valakut collects in your end step.
Goblin Bombardment variant: with Mishra's Bauble on the battlefield, sacrifice the animated Gruul Turf (it's a creature) to Bombardment for 1 damage, return the Bauble to hand with Turf's trigger, and recast it for {0} aiming the earthbend at Turf: infinite damage without another pinger.
Crop Rotation and Urza's Cave fetch Gruul Turf; Brightglass Gearhulk fetches Zuran Orb and Mishra's Bauble.

combos.title: Loop C: Ashaya + Toph, the Blind Bandit + Goblin Bombardment or Zuran Orb
combos.meta: Infinite damage or life and landfall · 3 cards, Toph not needed · {2}{G} for the Bandit
combos.text:
Needs: Ashaya on the battlefield (your nontoken creatures are Forest lands); Toph, the Blind Bandit in hand with {2}{G} (or Chord of Calling with X=3); Goblin Bombardment or Zuran Orb on the battlefield. It doesn't need Toph, and once set up it works at instant speed.
With Ashaya on the battlefield, cast Toph, the Blind Bandit: she enters as a land, one landfall.
Her enter trigger (earthbend 2) targets one of your lands: aim it at herself. She's left as a 2/2 with haste and will return if she dies.
Sacrifice her to Goblin Bombardment (1 damage to any target) or to Zuran Orb (2 life).
She returns tapped: another landfall and a legendary creature entering (Arbaaz Mir). Her enter trigger again: aim it at herself.
Repeat. With Bombardment, spread the damage among the three opponents; with the Orb you have infinite life and landfalls, and the pingers kill.
If the Bandit was already on the battlefield before Ashaya, animate her with Toph's earthbend in your end step (with Ashaya she's already a land), and start by sacrificing her.

combos.title: Bumi + Ashaya (infinite combats)
combos.meta: Infinite combats and land mana · 2 cards · 10 mana, Bumi must connect in every combat
combos.text:
Needs: Ashaya and Bumi on the battlefield, with Bumi free of summoning sickness; Bumi has to deal combat damage to a player in every combat. If Ashaya is already there when Bumi enters, his earthbend 4 can target Bumi itself (it's a land): he's left as a 4/4 with trample and haste (5/5 with Hardened Scales) and attacks that same turn. It's the only time it's worth animating Bumi.
Before combat, Secret Tunnel ({4}, tap) makes Bumi and another Human unblockable (The Earth King, Toph, the Blind Bandit, Toph, Hardheaded Teacher or Great Divide Guide): the connection is guaranteed.
Attack with Bumi at the opponent with the fewest blockers; trample pushes through the excess.
Bumi connects: all your lands untap, and with Ashaya that includes all your nontoken creatures. After that phase there is another combat in which only land creatures attack.
Under Ashaya, Bumi is a land creature: attack with him again, with your animated lands and with your creatures (they're all lands).
Repeat while Bumi connects: infinite combats and all your lands' mana each cycle. The Earth King fetches a basic for each attacker with power 4 or more: landfalls for the pingers.
Weak point: a fog effect, a very large blocker when the Tunnel isn't available, or removal on Bumi or Ashaya; keep Collective Resistance ready.

combos.title: Toph + Ragost + an animated artifact (engine every turn)
combos.meta: 3 to each opponent in each end step, plus cards or basics · 2 cards with Toph · {1} per activation
combos.text:
Needs: Toph and Ragost on the battlefield; an artifact worth sacrificing: Solemn Simulacrum (a card and a basic land), Heaped Harvest (two basic lands) or Ichor Wellspring (two cards); spare Treasures, Clues or rocks; a way to gain life each turn (Arbaaz Mir, Druid Class, Zuran Orb, Haywire Mite).
In your end step Toph animates the artifact; Ragost untaps at the same time if you gained life on your turn.
Activate Ragost ({1}, tap, sacrifice the animated artifact as a Food): 3 damage to each opponent.
The artifact gives its value when it dies (Solemn and Wellspring draw; Harvest fetches a basic land) and returns tapped: a landfall, its enter value again and Arbaaz Mir (1 to each opponent).
On each opponent's turn, gain at least 1 life before their end step: crack a fetch with Druid Class, sacrifice a land to Zuran Orb, or sacrifice Haywire Mite. At the beginning of that end step, Ragost untaps.
Activate it again there with a Treasure, a Clue (Tireless Tracker gets a counter) or a spare rock. With life gained each turn it's 3 to each opponent in every end step around the table: 12 to each opponent per full cycle.
Life gained during the end step doesn't untap Ragost that turn: gain it earlier. Keep a spare artifact to sacrifice in response to removal on Ragost.

combos.title: Animated Secret Tunnel + Seismic Tutelage (army finisher)
combos.meta: Kills a player in three attacks · 2 cards with Toph · {3}{G} + the previous turn's earthbend
combos.text:
Needs: Secret Tunnel on the battlefield; Toph (or Earthbender Ascension, Ba Sing Se or Toph, Hardheaded Teacher) to animate it; Seismic Tutelage in hand.
In your end step Toph animates Secret Tunnel: a 2/2 with haste (3/3 with Hardened Scales) that can't be blocked.
On your next turn, before combat, cast Seismic Tutelage on the Tunnel: one more counter (3 in total).
Attack: the counters double when it attacks (6), and the damage gets through with no block. Terrasymbiosis draws for the counters added.
Each attack doubles again: 3, 6, 12, 24; three attacks kill a 40-life player, sooner with Hardened Scales or if Toph animates it again in your end step (+2 before doubling).
From power 4 on, it also triggers The Earth King: one basic land per attack.
Never sacrifice it or use it for Harrow or Crop Rotation: it comes back without the Aura and without counters. Protect it with Origin of Metalbending or Collective Resistance.

cards.Toph, the First Metalbender: Your engine: cast her on turn 3 or 4 and never attack with her. With her on the battlefield, cast cheap artifacts after the pingers (each one is a landfall), and pick the land for each end-step earthbend carefully (see 'When to cast Toph'). Protect her on the turns her end step matters: the Coffin, a loop, Terrasymbiosis on the battlefield.
cards.Sol Ring: Turn 1 always: Toph on turn 3. If it arrives late, with Toph it's a landfall and an Arbaaz Mir trigger.
cards.Arcane Signet: Turn-2 rock that gives the color missing for Toph on turn 3. Late, with Toph, it's a landfall and an Arbaaz Mir trigger.
cards.Talisman of Impulse: Turn 2: red or green for Toph on turn 3 (1 damage per color). Late, cast it after a pinger: with Toph it's a cheap landfall.
cards.Talisman of Conviction: Turn 2: red or white, the colors most missing for Toph, Swords to Plowshares or Legion Guildmage. With Toph it's a landfall and an Arbaaz Mir trigger.
cards.Wayfarer's Bauble: Turn 1, and crack it on turn 2 for a basic. Later it's a target for Toph's earthbend: {2} for a basic, and it returns, two landfalls each turn.
cards.Solemn Simulacrum: Turn 4: a basic and, with Toph, two landfalls and an Arbaaz Mir trigger. It's the best earthbend target along with Ragost: sacrifice it as a Food (3 to each opponent), draw, and it returns and fetches another basic; Zuran Orb or Goblin Bombardment also work. With Toph it's a land, so it survives Planar Outburst.
cards.Rampant Growth: Turn 2: the basic of the color missing for Toph on turn 3. Late, cast it with the pingers on the battlefield.
cards.Shared Roots: Same as Rampant Growth on turn 2. It's a Lesson: with Toph, Hardheaded Teacher on the battlefield, the land it animates gets an extra counter.
cards.Sakura-Tribe Elder: Turn 2: block first, and sacrifice it before damage for a basic. If nobody attacks, sacrifice it at the end of the opponent's turn with a pinger on the battlefield.
cards.Lotus Cobra: Turn 2: each landfall gives you one mana; with a fetch and an artifact under Toph it pays for itself. It helps pay for the Coffin and is a piece of loop A with Springheart Nantuko. Don't risk it in blocks.
cards.Great Divide Guide: Turn 2: mana creature and color fixing. With Toph, all your artifact lands (the Coffin, the Baubles, Zuran Orb, Ichor Wellspring) and your Allies, Toph included, tap for mana of any color.
cards.Legion Guildmage: Turn 2 as a blocker. Late, each spare {5}{R} is 3 to each opponent (once per turn); with Fire Nation Archers, the excess becomes 5 to each opponent per turn. {2}{W}: tap a blocker before your attack, or an opponent's attacker at the beginning of their combat.
cards.Druid Class: Turn 2: 1 life per landfall, the life that untaps Ragost. Level up to 2 ({2}{G}) when you have spare lands in hand; level 3 ({4}{G}) is a late mana sink: a hasty land creature as big as your lands, an attacker for The Earth King.
cards.Crop Rotation: Game Changer, instant. Sacrifice the animated land (it returns, another landfall) for Gruul Turf (loop B), Urza's Cave, Secret Tunnel or Ba Sing Se, untapped. In response to removal on a key land, sacrifice it and get something back.
cards.Harrow: Instant: sacrifice the animated land (it returns) for two untapped basics: three landfalls; if the animated land is Heaped Harvest, it's five. Use it at the end of the turn of the opponent before you, or on your turn with the pingers on the battlefield.
cards.Cycle of Renewal: Like Harrow, but the basics enter tapped: use it at the end of an opponent's turn, on the animated land. It's a Lesson: an extra counter with Toph, Hardheaded Teacher.
cards.Heaped Harvest: Turn 3: a basic now and another when you sacrifice it. With Toph it's the best ramp target for earthbend: sacrifice it to Zuran Orb (free), Ragost (3 to each opponent) or its own {2}, and it returns: three landfalls and two basics per turn.
cards.Wood Elves: Turn 3: an untapped Forest, so you can cast another card the same turn. Later it's a green body for Chord of Calling's convoke and one more land with Ashaya.
cards.Tireless Provisioner: Turn 3: choose Treasure for each landfall (with Ragost they're Food too): mana on opponents' turns for instants and the Coffin, and ammunition for Ragost. A loop A piece with Springheart Nantuko.
cards.Earthbender Ascension: Turn 3: a basic and an animated 2/2 land. From the fourth landfall on, each land that enters puts a +1/+1 counter and trample on a creature: put it on Secret Tunnel or on The Earth King's attacker; Terrasymbiosis draws, and the Pantry accumulates.
cards.Wrenn and Realmbreaker: Alongside Toph or after her: all your artifact lands make any color. Use +1 each turn on a land that blocks (3/3 hexproof with vigilance), and −2 when you're missing a permanent. Don't expose it to an opposing army without blockers.
cards.Sabotender: Turn 2: each landfall is 1 to each opponent from the start. Cast it before the cheap artifacts, and before Toph if she can't come down a turn earlier. With reach it stops small fliers, but don't swap it out in a block.
cards.Arbaaz Mir: Cast it before the artifacts: with Toph, each artifact or legendary creature that enters is 1 to each opponent and 1 life, including the Coffin, the Baubles, Solemn and Heaped Harvest when they return animated. Recasting Toph, or casting Tannuk, Ragost or Annie Joins Up, also triggers it; its life untaps Ragost.
cards.Ragost, Deft Gastronaut: With it, every artifact is a Food: {1}, tap and sacrifice one = 3 to each opponent. Sacrifice Treasures and Clues first (each Clue gives Tireless Tracker a counter), then animated artifacts (they return). Activate it in each end step as soon as it untaps, and gain 1 life each turn before that end step.
cards.Goblin Bombardment: Sacrifice animated lands after Toph's earthbend: 1 damage, and they return, another landfall. In response to a board wipe or removal, sacrifice what's about to die; the Archers' Soldiers finish off the rest. The outlet of loop C and of loop B's variant.
cards.Fire Nation Archers: Turn 4 as a 3/4 blocker with reach that never attacks. Late, each spare {5} is 2 to each opponent and a 2/2 Soldier, with no tapping needed, at instant speed, and usable the turn it enters: spend all your mana at the end of the turn of the opponent before you. With infinite mana (loop A with Cobra and Provisioner) it kills without a pinger.
cards.Springheart Nantuko: Loop A piece: cast it with bestow ({1}{G}) on a Forest that Toph animated, with Cobra or Provisioner on the battlefield. Without the loop, on an animated land it copies that land for {1}{G} on each landfall (ramp that repeats), or leaves a 1/1 Insect per landfall. Chord of Calling doesn't work for the loop.
cards.Tannuk, Memorial Ensign: Turn 3: 1 to each opponent per landfall, and a card when there are two landfalls in the same turn. Look for that second landfall on opponents' turns too: a fetch or Harrow at the end of their turn makes you draw another card.
cards.Valakut Exploration: Turn 3 or 4, before a turn with many landfalls: each landfall exiles a card you can play, and whatever you don't play is damage to each opponent in your end step. In that end step, let its trigger resolve after Toph's earthbend and your sacrifices: those landfalls count too. With a loop it exiles your whole library: protect it until the end step, when that is already lethal.
cards.Tireless Tracker: Turn 3: one Clue per landfall. Crack them on opponents' turns with the spare mana; each Clue sacrificed (also to Ragost as Food) puts a counter on Tracker: Terrasymbiosis draws, and the Pantry accumulates.
cards.Zuran Orb: With Toph it's a land: one landfall for {0}. Sacrifice animated lands (they return), Heaped Harvest (a basic), or what's about to die to removal or Armageddon; each sacrifice gives 2 life, which untaps Ragost. A piece of loops B and C.
cards.Terrasymbiosis: Turn 3 with Toph nearby: her earthbend draws you 2 each turn (3 with Hardened Scales). It draws only once per turn, and it's optional: decline a small counter if a big one is coming that turn (Seismic Tutelage when attacking, Bumi, Planar Outburst's awaken).
cards.Stocking the Pantry: Turn 1 or alongside Toph: each earthbend, each Clue sacrificed with Tracker and each counter from Earthbender Ascension gives it a supply counter. Spend {2} per card with the spare mana at the end of the opponents' turns. Bad without a source of counters.
cards.Hardened Scales: Owner's card. Turn 1, or with Gearhulk: each earthbend puts one extra counter, so Toph's lands are 3/3, Terrasymbiosis draws 3, and the army grows by half. Alone it does nothing: if you have to choose, ramp comes first.
cards.Mishra's Bauble: With Toph it's a free landfall. Animated by Toph, crack it in that same end step: you draw in the next upkeep, and it returns as a land (another landfall and Arbaaz Mir). Look at the top card of the library of the opponent who is about to do something important.
cards.Soul-Guide Lantern: On entering, it exiles the card an opponent wants to reanimate; save it for that moment if an opponent plays from the graveyard. Sacrifice it ({1}) for a card, or for free to exile all opponents' graveyards. Animated by Toph, it returns and repeats each turn.
cards.Ichor Wellspring: Draws a card on entering and when it dies. Animated by Toph, sacrifice it to Ragost, Zuran Orb or Goblin Bombardment: two cards and a landfall each time. Gruul Turf can return it to hand to cast it again.
cards.Brightglass Gearhulk: Turn 5 or later ({G}{G}{W}{W}): fetches up to two of: Zuran Orb, Mishra's Bauble, Hardened Scales, Stocking the Pantry, Sol Ring, Soul-Guide Lantern, Wayfarer's Bauble or Haywire Mite; with loop B half-built, Zuran Orb first. It's a 4/4 with first strike and trample, a good attacker for The Earth King: never earthbend it.
cards.Seismic Sense: For {G}, look at as many cards as you have lands (with Toph, artifacts count too): use it from 6 lands to find a pinger, Springheart Nantuko, the loop piece you're missing or Gruul Turf. It's a Lesson: with Toph, Hardheaded Teacher, it animates with an extra counter.
cards.Chord of Calling: Instant: cast it at the end of the turn of the opponent before you, with convoke from animated lands and green creatures. X=2 Lotus Cobra or a pinger, X=3 Provisioner, Tannuk or the Bandit, X=4 Archers or Solemn, X=5 Ashaya or Bumi; X=1 Haywire Mite in response. Bad early.
cards.Toph, Hardheaded Teacher: Turn 4 or 5: on entering, discard a spare land and return Harrow, Crop Rotation, Chord of Calling or a removal spell. Each spell you cast animates a land (with an extra counter if it's a Lesson): that's how you animate the Coffin and a valuable artifact the same turn. The hub of loop B with Gruul Turf and Zuran Orb.
cards.The Earth King: Tested by the deck owner. Turn 4: leaves a 4/4 Bear, and each attack with creatures of power 4 or more (the Bear, Gearhulk, Bumi, a big animated land) fetches that many basics: landfalls for the pingers. Attack where the Bear survives or where its death doesn't matter.
cards.Toph, the Blind Bandit: Turn 3: animates a land with two counters (another sacrifice target that returns), and her power counts all the counters on your lands: she's an attacker for The Earth King. Loop C piece: with Ashaya already on the battlefield, cast her afterward, so her earthbend targets herself.
cards.Seismic Tutelage: Tested by the deck owner; bad early. Put it on an animated Secret Tunnel (unblockable) or on the Bear, never on a land you plan to sacrifice: its counters double on each attack (3, 6, 12, 24), and three attacks kill a player. Terrasymbiosis draws for the doubled counters.
cards.Bumi, Unleashed: Turn 5 or later: his earthbend 4 creates a 4/4 haste attacker for The Earth King. Don't aim it at Bumi unless Ashaya is on the battlefield (there it gives him haste). If he connects, you untap all your lands, and the animated lands attack again. With Ashaya, it's infinite combats.
cards.Ashaya, Soul of the Wild: Turn 5 or later: each creature you cast is a landfall, and your nontoken creatures survive Planar Outburst. With Bumi (infinite combats), or with the Bandit and Goblin Bombardment or Zuran Orb (loop C), it wins by itself. Never earthbend it: it loses its size.
cards.Annie Joins Up: Turn 5 or later: 5 damage to the creature or planeswalker that bothers you most, and from then on each trigger of your legendary creatures is doubled: Toph animates two lands (the Coffin and a valuable artifact), Tannuk and Arbaaz Mir trigger twice, and The Earth King fetches double. It's legendary, so Arbaaz Mir triggers when it enters.
cards.Swords to Plowshares: {W} at any time: exile the commander or the engine that's beating you. Don't spend it on a big creature that the Coffin or an animated blocker already handles.
cards.Path to Exile: Like Swords to Plowshares, but the opponent searches for a land: use it first in long games, when one more land doesn't matter to them, and save Swords to Plowshares for the early turns.
cards.Fateful Absence: {1}{W} instant for a creature or planeswalker. The opponent gets a Clue, so use it on something that matters; it's your best answer to a planeswalker.
cards.Haywire Mite: Hold it while there's no annoying opposing artifact or enchantment. {G} and sacrificing it exiles one at instant speed and gives you 2 life (Ragost untaps). Animated by Toph, it returns, so it can be used again each time you animate it.
cards.Collective Resistance: Hold it as a shield: hexproof and indestructible for Toph, a pinger or a loop piece, and one of the few things that stops a targeted exile. If you don't need a shield that turn, destroy an artifact or enchantment (or both, with escalate).
cards.Origin of Metalbending: {1}{G} shield: indestructible and a +1/+1 counter (Terrasymbiosis draws) for Toph or a loop piece, against destruction or damage. If you don't need it, destroy an artifact or enchantment. It's a Lesson for Toph, Hardheaded Teacher.
cards.Beast Within: Instant for any permanent, including a land or a combo piece: keep it open from turn 5. The opponent gets a 3/3; on the turn of their combo, that doesn't matter.
cards.Stroke of Midnight: Instant for any nonland permanent, and the opponent gets only a 1/1: use it on the artifact, enchantment or commander that threatens you most.
cards.Chaos Warp: Your instant-speed answer to any permanent: enchantments, planeswalkers, stax pieces. Its owner reveals another card that may enter: use it on threats worth that risk.
cards.Drannith Magistrate: Game Changer. Turn 2 against commander tables: no opponent casts their commander from the command zone, nor anything from the graveyard or exile. It draws the removal that won't go to your pingers.
cards.Planar Outburst: Your only sweeper: only creatures that aren't lands die, so your animated lands survive (and with Ashaya, all your nontoken creatures). Use it when you're behind on board, ideally with Make a Stand first. Bad early.
cards.Redirect Lightning: {R} plus {2} or 5 life: redirect a removal spell to Toph or a pinger, or a counterspell to your loop piece (aimed at Redirect itself). Keep it for the loop turn; it's a Lesson for Toph, Hardheaded Teacher.
cards.Make a Stand: Against a destruction or damage board wipe, cast it in response: your team survives. Cast it before your own Planar Outburst, and only the opposing creatures die. Bad early.
cards.The Stasis Coffin: Owner's card. Cast it with {2} free (5 mana that turn). With Toph, animate it in your end step and activate it: protection from everything until your next turn, and it returns tapped (a landfall and Arbaaz Mir). It protects you, not your permanents, and doesn't stop life loss or mill; without Toph it's single use.
cards.Command Tower: Any of the three colors: your best first land.
cards.Exotic Orchard: Makes the colors that opponents' lands can make; early, play a land whose output you know first.
cards.Ba Sing Se: Enters untapped if you control a basic land. Late, {2}{G} and tap: earthbend 2 as a sorcery, a second earthbend target for the turn, and counters for Terrasymbiosis and the Pantry.
cards.Rootbound Crag: Enters untapped with a Mountain or a Forest: play it from turn 2.
cards.Sunpetal Grove: Enters untapped with a Forest or a Plains: play it from turn 2.
cards.Clifftop Retreat: Enters untapped with a Mountain or a Plains: play it from turn 2.
cards.Game Trail: Reveal a Mountain or a Forest from hand so it enters untapped.
cards.Fortified Village: Reveal a Forest or a Plains from hand so it enters untapped.
cards.Furycalm Snarl: Reveal a Mountain or a Plains from hand so it enters untapped.
cards.Rugged Prairie: Filter: with another red or white source it makes {R}{W}, {R}{R} or {W}{W}. Don't play it as your only colored land.
cards.Battlefield Forge: Red or white for 1 damage; colorless for free.
cards.Secret Tunnel: Colorless. Animate it with Toph and put Seismic Tutelage on it: an unblockable attacker that grows. {4} and tap: two creatures that share a type (Bumi and The Earth King, Humans) can't be blocked.
cards.Urza's Cave: Colorless and untapped. {3}, tap and sacrifice: any land (Gruul Turf for loop B, Secret Tunnel, a fetch); animated by Toph, it returns and repeats each turn.
cards.Gruul Turf: Enters tapped and returns a land to your hand: early, a basic you replay; with Toph, an artifact (Heaped Harvest, Solemn Simulacrum, Ichor Wellspring) to recast for value. Loop B piece; never play it as your only land.
cards.Evolving Wilds: Crack it at the end of an opponent's turn or with pingers on the battlefield: two landfalls, three if Toph animated it before cracking.
cards.Terramorphic Expanse: Like Evolving Wilds: crack it when more pingers are on the battlefield, and animate it with Toph so it returns.
cards.Vibrant Cityscape: Another fetch for a basic: two landfalls, three if Toph animated it before cracking.
cards.Forest: Ten copies: the green for almost the whole deck, and the best earthbend target for loop A with Springheart Nantuko.
cards.Mountain: Five copies: Toph's red and the pingers; they activate Rootbound Crag, Clifftop Retreat and Game Trail.
cards.Plains: Six copies: Toph's white, the removal and Brightglass Gearhulk; they activate Sunpetal Grove and Fortified Village.
